name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Incomplete digestive system in Platyhelminthes

questiontext.text: In which of the following animal phyla does the digestive system have only a single opening to the outside of the body that serves as both mouth and anus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An incomplete digestive system has only a single opening to the exterior that functions as both mouth and anus, whereas a complete digestive system has two separate openings (mouth and anus).

Step 2: Application
Members of Phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms) possess an incomplete digestive system with a single opening. Higher phyla such as Aschelminthes, Annelida, and Arthropoda possess a complete digestive system.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The phylum characterised by a single opening serving as both mouth and anus is Platyhelminthes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - Open type circulatory system definition

questiontext.text: A circulatory system in which blood is pumped out of the heart and the cells and tissues are directly bathed in it is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal circulatory systems are broadly classified into open and closed types based on whether blood remains confined within blood vessels.

Step 2: Application
In an open circulatory system, blood is pumped out of the heart into open spaces where cells and tissues are directly bathed in it. In contrast, a closed circulatory system circulates blood through a series of vessels of varying diameters (arteries, veins, and capillaries).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The described pattern is the open type of circulatory system.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q03 - Freshwater sponge example in Porifera

questiontext.text: Although most members of Phylum Porifera are marine, which of the following is a freshwater sponge?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sponges (Phylum Porifera) are predominantly marine, asymmetrical multicellular animals, with a notable freshwater representative.

Step 2: Application
Among the common examples of Porifera, Sycon (Scypha) and Euspongia (Bath sponge) are marine, whereas Spongilla is a freshwater sponge. Adamsia (sea anemone) belongs to Coelenterata.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The freshwater sponge is Spongilla.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q04 - Functions of cnidoblasts in Coelenterata

questiontext.text: Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) present on the tentacles and body of cnidarians are primarily used for:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria) derives its name from specialised stinging cells called cnidoblasts or cnidocytes, which contain stinging capsules (nematocysts).

Step 2: Application
Cnidoblasts are used for anchorage, defense, and the capture of prey. Osmoregulation and excretion are performed by flame cells or nephridia in other phyla, while intracellular digestion in sponges is aided by choanocytes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The primary functions of cnidoblasts are anchorage, defense, and capture of prey.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q05 - Bioluminescence in Phylum Ctenophora

questiontext.text: Bioluminescence—the property of a living organism to emit light—is well-marked in members of which phylum?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain marine invertebrates possess the physiological ability to emit light, a phenomenon termed bioluminescence.

Step 2: Application
In Phylum Ctenophora (sea walnuts or comb jellies, such as Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana), bioluminescence is a well-marked characteristic feature.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Bioluminescence is well-marked in Ctenophora.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q06 - High regeneration capacity in Planaria

questiontext.text: Which of the following flatworms is well known for possessing a high regeneration capacity?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Platyhelminthes includes parasitic flatworms like tapeworms and liver flukes as well as free-living forms capable of regenerating lost body parts.

Step 2: Application
Planaria, a member of Platyhelminthes, possesses high regeneration capacity. Taenia (tapeworm) and Fasciola (liver fluke) are endoparasites, while Ascaris is a roundworm (Aschelminthes).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The flatworm with high regeneration capacity is Planaria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q07 - Largest phylum of Kingdom Animalia

questiontext.text: Over two-thirds of all named species on earth belong to which largest phylum of Kingdom Animalia?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Kingdom Animalia comprises various phyla differing vastly in species diversity.

Step 2: Application
Phylum Arthropoda (which includes insects) is the largest phylum of Animalia, accounting for over two-thirds of all named species on earth. Mollusca is the second largest animal phylum.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The largest phylum of Kingdom Animalia is Arthropoda.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q08 - Second largest animal phylum

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the second largest animal phylum?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Among animal phyla, Arthropoda is the largest, followed by another coelomate, unsegmented, soft-bodied phylum.

Step 2: Application
Phylum Mollusca is the second largest animal phylum, consisting of terrestrial or aquatic animals with a calcareous shell and distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The second largest animal phylum is Mollusca.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q09 - Water vascular system in Echinodermata

questiontext.text: The presence of a water vascular system—which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration—is the most distinctive feature of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Distinctive organ systems characterise specific phyla; sponges have a water canal system, whereas spiny-bodied marine coelomates possess a water vascular system.

Step 2: Application
Echinoderms (such as Asterias and Ophiura) possess a water vascular system that functions in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The water vascular system is the most distinctive feature of Echinodermata.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q10 - Unique characteristics of Class Mammalia

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most unique characteristic of Class Mammalia?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
While traits like a four-chambered heart and homoiothermy are shared by both Aves and Mammalia, certain integumentary glands are exclusive to mammals.

Step 2: Application
The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk-producing mammary glands by which the young ones are nourished, along with hair on the skin and external ears (pinnae).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The presence of milk-producing mammary glands is the most unique characteristic of Class Mammalia.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q11 - Radial symmetry in animal phyla

questiontext.text: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Which group of phyla exhibits this body plan?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal body symmetry is categorised into asymmetrical, radial symmetry, and bilateral symmetry.

Step 2: Application
Coelenterates, ctenophores, and adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry. Annelids, arthropods, platyhelminthes, and chordates exhibit bilateral symmetry, while sponges are mostly asymmetrical.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Radial symmetry is exhibited by Coelenterata, Ctenophora, and adult Echinodermata.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q12 - Metameric segmentation in earthworm

questiontext.text: In earthworm, the body is externally and internally divided into segments with a serial repetition of at least some organs. This phenomenon is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Body segmentation can be superficial or true metameric segmentation involving both external and internal division.

Step 2: Application
In earthworms (Annelida), the external and internal division of the body into segments with serial repetition of at least some organs is called metameric segmentation, and the phenomenon is termed metamerism. Metagenesis refers to alternation of generation in cnidarians.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The phenomenon is known as metamerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q13 - Embryonic origin and position of notochord

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the embryonic origin and anatomical position of the notochord in chordates?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The notochord is a defining diagnostic structure of Phylum Chordata formed during embryonic development.

Step 2: Application
The notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development. Animals lacking this structure are non-chordates (Porifera to Echinoderms).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development.

answer.text: It is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side.
It is an ectodermally derived hollow tube formed on the dorsal side.
It is an endodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the ventral side.
It is a mesodermally derived solid cord formed on the ventral side.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q14 - Digestion and reproduction in Porifera

questiontext.text: Which of the following combinations of features is true for members of Phylum Porifera?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sponges are primitive multicellular animals with cellular level of organisation and characteristic reproductive and digestive physiology.

Step 2: Application
In sponges, digestion is intracellular, sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), fertilisation is internal, and development is indirect with a morphologically distinct larval stage. Their body is supported by spicules or spongin fibres.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Sponges exhibit intracellular digestion, hermaphroditism, internal fertilisation, and indirect development.

answer.text: Extracellular digestion, dioecious, external fertilisation, direct development
Intracellular digestion, hermaphrodite, internal fertilisation, indirect development
Intracellular digestion, dioecious, external fertilisation, indirect development
Extracellular digestion, hermaphrodite, internal fertilisation, direct development

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q15 - Calcium carbonate skeleton and hypostome in Cnidaria

questiontext.text: In Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria), the mouth is located on the ______ and corals possess a skeleton composed of ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cnidarians possess a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening and, in certain colonial forms like corals, a hard mineralised skeleton.

Step 2: Application
In cnidarians, the single opening (mouth) is situated on an elevated structure called the hypostome. Corals secrete a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The mouth is located on the hypostome, and corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q16 - Reproduction and habitat of Ctenophora

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Phylum Ctenophora?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ctenophores (sea walnuts or comb jellies) are exclusively marine, radially symmetrical, diploblastic organisms with tissue level of organisation.

Step 2: Application
Ctenophores bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, exhibit both extracellular and intracellular digestion, have united sexes (not separate), and reproduce only by sexual means with external fertilisation and indirect development. Therefore, claiming they reproduce asexually by fragmentation is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that ctenophores reproduce primarily by asexual fragmentation.

answer.text: Reproduction takes place primarily by asexual fragmentation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q17 - Parasitic adaptations in Platyhelminthes

questiontext.text: Which of the following features are characteristic adaptations of parasitic forms in Phylum Platyhelminthes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Most flatworms (Phylum Platyhelminthes) are endoparasites found in animals, including humans, and possess specific morphological and physiological adaptations for parasitism.

Step 2: Application
Parasitic flatworms possess hooks and suckers for attachment to the host, and some absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface. They also have flame cells for osmoregulation and excretion, but lack parapodia or radula.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Presence of hooks and suckers, and direct absorption of nutrients through the body surface, are characteristic adaptations of parasitic Platyhelminthes.

answer.text: Presence of hooks and suckers, and direct absorption of nutrients through the body surface
Presence of parapodia and closed circulatory system
Presence of Malpighian tubules and chitinous exoskeleton

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q18 - Muscular pharynx and dioecious nature of Aschelminthes

questiontext.text: In Phylum Aschelminthes (roundworms), the alimentary canal is complete with a well-developed ______, and sexes are ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aschelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, pseudocoelomate animals with an organ-system level of organisation.

Step 2: Application
Roundworms have a complete alimentary canal featuring a well-developed muscular pharynx. Their sexes are separate (dioecious), with males and females being distinct, and females are often longer than males.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Aschelminthes possess a muscular pharynx and separate sexes (dioecious).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q19 - Parapodia and sexuality in Phylum Annelida

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements about Phylum Annelida is TRUE?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Annelida includes aquatic and terrestrial segmented coelomates with closed circulation and diverse reproductive habits.

Step 2: Application
Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages called parapodia that help in swimming, and Nereis is dioecious, whereas earthworms (Pheretima) and leeches (Hirudinaria) are monoecious. Annelids have a closed circulatory system and longitudinal and circular muscles for locomotion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Nereis is dioecious and possesses lateral appendages called parapodia for swimming.

answer.text: All annelids are monoecious and lack a circulatory system.
Pheretima possesses parapodia for swimming and is dioecious.
Nereis is dioecious and possesses lateral appendages called parapodia for swimming.
Annelids have an open circulatory system and pseudocoelom.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q20 - Neural system of Phylum Annelida

questiontext.text: How is the neural system organised in members of Phylum Annelida?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Non-chordates such as annelids possess a ventral, solid, and double central nervous system.

Step 2: Application
Specifically, the neural system of annelids consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The annelid neural system consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord.

answer.text: Single dorsal hollow nerve cord without ganglia
Diffused nerve net without a central nerve cord
Paired ganglia connected to a single dorsal solid nerve cord
Paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q21 - Respiratory organs in Phylum Arthropoda

questiontext.text: Which of the following sets includes ONLY the respiratory organs found in Phylum Arthropoda?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Because arthropods inhabit aquatic, terrestrial, and aerial environments, they have evolved diverse respiratory structures.

Step 2: Application
Respiratory organs in Arthropoda are gills, book gills, book lungs, or the tracheal system. Malpighian tubules are excretory organs, and proboscis glands belong to Hemichordata.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The respiratory organs of Arthropoda are gills, book gills, book lungs, and tracheal system.

answer.text: Gills, book gills, book lungs, and tracheal system
Gills, Malpighian tubules, book lungs, and flame cells
Book gills, nephridia, tracheal system, and proboscis gland
Book lungs, radula, gills, and air sacs

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q22 - Balancing organs in Arthropoda

questiontext.text: In arthropods, which sensory structures function as balancing organs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arthropods possess well-developed sensory organs including antennae, simple and compound eyes, and equilibrium receptors.

Step 2: Application
Statocysts serve as balancing organs in arthropods. Malpighian tubules are excretory, ommatidia/compound eyes are photoreceptive, and radula is a molluscan feeding organ.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The balancing organs in arthropods are statocysts.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q23 - Mantle cavity and gills in Mollusca

questiontext.text: In Phylum Mollusca, the space between the visceral hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity, in which feather-like gills are present. What are the functions of these gills?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In molluscs, a soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump, enclosing the mantle cavity containing feather-like gills.

Step 2: Application
These feather-like gills in the mantle cavity perform both respiratory and excretory functions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The feather-like gills in molluscs have respiratory and excretory functions.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q24 - Digestive and excretory features of Echinodermata

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly describes the digestive and excretory systems in Phylum Echinodermata?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Echinoderms are marine coelomates with an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and a unique orientation of their complete alimentary canal.

Step 2: Application
In Echinodermata, the digestive system is complete with the mouth on the lower (ventral) side and the anus on the upper (dorsal) side, and an excretory system is completely absent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Echinoderms have a complete digestive system with a ventral mouth and dorsal anus, and they lack an excretory system.

answer.text: Complete digestive system with dorsal mouth and ventral anus; excretion by flame cells
Complete digestive system with ventral mouth and dorsal anus; excretory system absent

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q25 - Body plan and circulation of Hemichordata

questiontext.text: Members of Phylum Hemichordata (such as Balanoglossus) have a cylindrical body composed of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hemichordata is a small phylum of worm-like, marine, coelomate non-chordate animals with an open circulatory system and gill respiration.

Step 2: Application
Their cylindrical body is divided into three distinct regions: an anterior proboscis, a collar (containing the rudimentary stomochord), and a long trunk.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The body of hemichordates is composed of an anterior proboscis, a collar, and a long trunk.

answer.text: Head, trunk, and post-anal tail with notochord

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q26 - Comparison of Chordates and Non-chordates

questiontext.text: Which of the following contrasts between chordates and non-chordates is CORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chordates and non-chordates differ fundamentally in the position and structure of their central nervous system, heart, notochord, gill slits, and post-anal tail.

Step 2: Application
In chordates, the central nervous system is dorsal, hollow, and single, and the heart is ventral. In non-chordates, the central nervous system is ventral, solid, and double, and the heart (if present) is dorsal. Furthermore, chordates have pharyngeal gill slits and a post-anal tail.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct contrast is that chordates have a dorsal, hollow, single central nervous system and a ventral heart, whereas non-chordates have a ventral, solid, double central nervous system and a dorsal heart (if present).

answer.text: Chordates have a ventral solid CNS and dorsal heart; non-chordates have a dorsal hollow CNS and ventral heart.
Chordates have a dorsal, hollow, single CNS and ventral heart; non-chordates have a ventral, solid, double CNS and dorsal heart (if present).
Chordates lack a post-anal part; non-chordates possess a post-anal tail.
Chordates have an unperforated pharynx; non-chordates have paired pharyngeal gill slits.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q27 - Notochord distribution in Protochordates

questiontext.text: In subphylum Urochordata (Tunicata), the notochord is present ______, whereas in subphylum Cephalochordata, it ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Subphyla Urochordata and Cephalochordata are collectively referred to as protochordates and are exclusively marine, differing in the extent and persistence of the notochord.

Step 2: Application
In Urochordata (e.g., Ascidia), the notochord is present only in the larval tail. In Cephalochordata (e.g., Branchiostoma), the notochord extends from the head to the tail region and is persistent throughout life.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In Urochordata the notochord is present only in the larval tail, whereas in Cephalochordata it extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.

answer.text: Throughout life from head to tail; is absent in adults
Only in the adult collar region; is replaced by a vertebral column
Only in the larval tail; extends from head to tail and is persistent throughout life
Only in the embryonic head; disappears before larval stage

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q28 - Characteristics of Class Cyclostomata

questiontext.text: Which of the following features accurately describes living members of Class Cyclostomata?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Cyclostomata represents Division Agnatha (jawless vertebrates) and includes primitive marine ectoparasites such as Petromyzon and Myxine.

Step 2: Application
Cyclostomes have an elongated body bearing 6–15 pairs of gill slits for respiration, a sucking and circular mouth without jaws, and a body devoid of scales and paired fins. Their cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous, and circulation is of closed type.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws, 6–15 pairs of gill slits, and a body devoid of scales and paired fins.

answer.text: Powerful jaws, placoid scales, and paired pelvic fins with claspers
Four pairs of gills covered by an operculum and bony endoskeleton
Open circulatory system and 2–4 pairs of gill slits
Sucking and circular mouth without jaws, 6–15 pairs of gill slits, and absence of scales and paired fins

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q29 - Teeth and mouth position in Chondrichthyes

questiontext.text: In cartilaginous fishes (Class Chondrichthyes), the mouth is located ______ and the teeth are modified ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chondrichthyes are marine predaceous fishes with a streamlined body, cartilaginous endoskeleton, and tough skin.

Step 2: Application
Their mouth is located ventrally, and their skin contains minute placoid scales. Their teeth are modified placoid scales that are backwardly directed.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In Chondrichthyes, the mouth is ventral and teeth are modified placoid scales.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q30 - Gill cover and scales in Osteichthyes

questiontext.text: Members of Class Osteichthyes (bony fishes) possess four pairs of gills covered by an ______ on each side, and their skin is covered with ______ scales.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Osteichthyes includes both marine and freshwater fishes with a bony endoskeleton and mostly terminal mouth.

Step 2: Application
Bony fishes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum (gill cover) on each side, and their skin is covered with cycloid or ctenoid scales (unlike placoid scales in Chondrichthyes).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Osteichthyes possess an operculum and cycloid/ctenoid scales.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q31 - Cloaca and respiration in Class Amphibia

questiontext.text: In amphibians, the alimentary canal, urinary tract, and reproductive tract open into a common chamber called the ______, and respiration occurs by ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amphibians are tetrapods adapted to live in both aquatic and terrestrial habitats, with moist scaleless skin.

Step 2: Application
In amphibians, the alimentary, urinary, and reproductive tracts open into a common chamber called the cloaca, which opens to the exterior. Respiration takes place by gills, lungs, and through the moist skin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The common chamber is the cloaca, and respiration occurs by gills, lungs, and through skin.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q32 - Ear structure and skin cast in Reptilia

questiontext.text: Which of the following is true regarding the sensory organs and skin of reptiles?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reptiles are mostly terrestrial, creeping or crawling poikilotherms with dry, cornified skin.

Step 2: Application
Reptiles do not have external ear openings (pinnae); instead, a tympanum represents the ear. Their body is covered by dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes, and snakes and lizards shed their scales as a skin cast.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Reptiles lack external ear openings (tympanum represents the ear), and snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast.

answer.text: They possess external ear pinnae and moist scaleless skin.
They have external ear openings and an oil gland at the base of the tail.
They possess placoid scales and external fertilisation.
They lack external ear openings (tympanum represents ear), and snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q33 - Digestive chambers and skin gland in Aves

questiontext.text: In birds (Class Aves), the digestive tract has two additional chambers called ______, and the skin is dry without glands except the ______ at the base of the tail.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Birds exhibit specialised anatomical features in both their digestive system and integument.

Step 2: Application
The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers—the crop and gizzard—for storing and grinding food. Their skin is dry and devoid of glands except for the oil gland at the base of the tail.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The additional digestive chambers are crop and gizzard, and the skin gland at the base of the tail is the oil gland.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q34 - Homoiothermous vertebrate classes

questiontext.text: Which pair of vertebrate classes consists exclusively of warm-blooded (homoiothermous) animals capable of maintaining a constant body temperature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrates are either poikilothermous (cold-blooded, lacking the capacity to regulate body temperature) or homoiothermous (warm-blooded, able to maintain a constant body temperature).

Step 2: Application
Fishes (Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes), amphibians, and reptiles are poikilothermous. Only birds (Aves) and mammals (Mammalia) are homoiothermous.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pair of homoiothermous vertebrate classes is Aves and Mammalia.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q35 - Polyp and medusa forms in Coelenterata

questiontext.text: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding body forms and alternation of generation in Phylum Coelenterata:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms: polyp (sessile and cylindrical) and medusa (umbrella-shaped and free-swimming).

Step 2: Application
Hydra and Adamsia exist in the sessile, cylindrical polyp form, whereas Aurelia (jelly fish) exists in the umbrella-shaped, free-swimming medusa form. In Obelia, both forms occur with metagenesis (polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form polyps sexually). Therefore, claiming Aurelia is a sessile cylindrical polyp is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that Aurelia is a sessile, cylindrical polyp form.

answer.text: Adamsia exhibits the sessile, cylindrical polyp body form.
In Obelia, polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form polyps sexually.
Aurelia (jelly fish) is a sessile, cylindrical polyp form.
Digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q36 - Fertilisation and development across early non-chordates

questiontext.text: Compare fertilisation and development among Porifera, Ctenophora, and Platyhelminthes. Which combination is completely accurate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Early non-chordate phyla differ in whether fertilisation is internal or external, though many share indirect development involving larval stages.

Step 2: Application
1. In Porifera, fertilisation is internal and development is indirect (with a morphologically distinct larval stage).
2. In Ctenophora, fertilisation is external with indirect development.
3. In Platyhelminthes, fertilisation is internal and development occurs through many larval stages (indirect).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All three phyla exhibit indirect development, with internal fertilisation in Porifera and Platyhelminthes and external fertilisation in Ctenophora.

answer.text: Porifera: external, direct; Ctenophora: internal, indirect; Platyhelminthes: external, indirect
Porifera: internal, direct; Ctenophora: external, direct; Platyhelminthes: internal, direct
Porifera: external, indirect; Ctenophora: external, direct; Platyhelminthes: internal, indirect
Porifera: internal, indirect; Ctenophora: external, indirect; Platyhelminthes: internal, indirect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q37 - Distinguishing Platyhelminthes and Aschelminthes parasites

questiontext.text: A student examines four parasitic worms: Taenia, Fasciola, Wuchereria, and Ancylostoma. Which pair possesses a pseudocoelom and a complete alimentary canal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Parasitic helminths belong to either Phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms) or Phylum Aschelminthes (roundworms), which differ in coelom and digestive tract completeness.

Step 2: Application
Taenia (tapeworm) and Fasciola (liver fluke) belong to Platyhelminthes, which are acoelomate with an incomplete digestive system. Wuchereria (filaria worm) and Ancylostoma (hookworm) belong to Aschelminthes, which are pseudocoelomate with a complete alimentary canal.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pair possessing a pseudocoelom and a complete alimentary canal is Wuchereria and Ancylostoma.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q38 - Presence of segmentation across animal phyla

questiontext.text: According to the salient features of animal phyla, body segmentation is present in which of the following groups?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Segmentation is a key diagnostic feature used in the comparative classification of Kingdom Animalia.

Step 2: Application
Body segmentation is present in Annelida (first observed here), Arthropoda, and Chordata. It is absent in Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Mollusca, Echinodermata, and Hemichordata.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Segmentation is present in Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q39 - Identifying non-arthropod among marine and terrestrial examples

questiontext.text: Which of the following animals does NOT belong to Phylum Arthropoda?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Careful distinction of generic names across Arthropoda and Mollusca is essential in animal classification.

Step 2: Application
Limulus (king crab), Locusta (locust), and Laccifer (lac insect) all belong to Phylum Arthropoda. In contrast, Loligo (squid) belongs to Phylum Mollusca.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The animal that does not belong to Phylum Arthropoda is Loligo.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q40 - Comprehensive profile of Balanoglossus

questiontext.text: Which set of characteristics accurately describes Balanoglossus (Phylum Hemichordata)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hemichordates are worm-like marine non-chordates that share a superficial notochord-like structure (stomochord) in the collar region.

Step 2: Application
Balanoglossus possesses a stomochord in the collar region, an open circulatory system, gill respiration, a proboscis gland as the excretory organ, separate sexes, external fertilisation, and indirect development.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate profile for Balanoglossus is stomochord in collar, open circulatory system, gill respiration, proboscis gland for excretion, and external fertilisation.

answer.text: True notochord, closed circulatory system, book gills, nephridia, internal fertilisation
Stomochord, closed circulatory system, tracheal system, Malpighian tubules, direct development
True notochord, open circulatory system, skin respiration, flame cells, external fertilisation
Stomochord in collar, open circulatory system, gill respiration, proboscis gland for excretion, external fertilisation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q41 - Classification of Urochordata and Cephalochordata examples

questiontext.text: Identify the group of animals that belongs exclusively to Subphylum Urochordata (Tunicata):

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protochordates are divided into Urochordata (Tunicata) and Cephalochordata.

Step 2: Application
Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum are examples of Urochordata. Branchiostoma (Amphioxus or Lancelet) is an example of Cephalochordata, while Petromyzon and Myxine belong to Vertebrata (Cyclostomata).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The group belonging exclusively to Urochordata is Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q42 - Contrasting Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes

questiontext.text: Which of the following features is characteristic of Chondrichthyes rather than Osteichthyes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Superclass Pisces is divided into Class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) and Class Osteichthyes (bony fishes), which differ in skeletal, reproductive, and gill structures.

Step 2: Application
In Chondrichthyes, the notochord is persistent throughout life, gill slits are separate without an operculum, pelvic fins in males bear claspers, fertilisation is internal, and many are viviparous. In contrast, Osteichthyes have an operculum, air bladder, usually external fertilisation, and are mostly oviparous.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Male pelvic fins bearing claspers, internal fertilisation, and absence of an operculum are characteristic of Chondrichthyes.

answer.text: Presence of an air bladder and external fertilisation
Male pelvic fins bearing claspers, internal fertilisation, and gill slits without operculum
Terminal mouth, cycloid scales, and direct development with oviparity
Four pairs of gills covered by an operculum and bony endoskeleton

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q43 - Habitat classification of Osteichthyes examples

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly pairs the habitat or category of bony fishes (Osteichthyes) with its examples?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Osteichthyes includes marine, freshwater, and aquarium bony fishes.

Step 2: Application
Marine bony fishes include Exocoetus (flying fish) and Hippocampus (sea horse). Freshwater bony fishes include Labeo (rohu), Catla (katla), and Clarias (magur). Aquarium fishes include Betta (fighting fish) and Pterophyllum (angel fish).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate pairing is Marine: Exocoetus, Hippocampus; Freshwater: Labeo, Catla; Aquarium: Betta, Pterophyllum.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q44 - Heart chamber evolution across Vertebrata

questiontext.text: Select the group of vertebrates in which ALL listed members possess a completely four-chambered heart:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrates have a ventral muscular heart with two, three, or four chambers depending on the taxonomic class and specific exceptions.

Step 2: Application
1. Fishes (Scoliodon, Labeo) have a two-chambered heart.
2. Amphibians (Rana, Salamandra) and most reptiles (Chameleon, Naja, Chelone) have a three-chambered heart.
3. Crocodiles (Crocodilus), all birds (e.g., Corvus, Pavo), and all mammals (e.g., Balaenoptera, Ornithorhynchus) possess a four-chambered heart.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The group in which all listed members have a four-chambered heart is Crocodilus, Corvus, and Balaenoptera.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q45 - Poisonous snakes in Class Reptilia

questiontext.text: Which of the following lists consists exclusively of poisonous snakes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Reptilia includes turtles, tortoises, lizards, crocodiles, and snakes, among which specific genera are venomous.

Step 2: Application
The poisonous snakes cited in NCERT Class Reptilia are Naja (cobra), Bangarus (krait), and Vipera (viper). Chelone (turtle), Testudo (tortoise), Calotes (garden lizard), and Hemidactylus (wall lizard) are non-snake reptiles.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The list consisting exclusively of poisonous snakes is Naja, Bangarus, and Vipera.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q46 - Flightless birds and respiratory adaptations in Aves

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements about Class Aves is INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Aves is characterised by feathers, wings modified from forelimbs, pneumatic bones, and efficient lung respiration supplemented by air sacs.

Step 2: Application
Birds are warm-blooded, oviparous with internal fertilisation and direct development, and most can fly except flightless birds such as Struthio (ostrich). Birds do NOT exhibit viviparity; all birds are oviparous.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that flightless birds like Struthio are viviparous.

answer.text: Air sacs connected to lungs supplement respiration.
Forelimbs are modified into wings, and hind limbs generally have scales.
Endoskeleton is fully ossified with hollow pneumatic long bones.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q47 - Aquatic and flying mammals in Class Mammalia

questiontext.text: Balaenoptera (Blue whale), Delphinus (Common dolphin), and Pteropus (Flying fox) are adapted to aquatic or aerial life, yet they are placed in Class Mammalia because they share:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Despite habitat-specific limb adaptations (swimming or flying), all mammals share fundamental mammalian traits.

Step 2: Application
Balaenoptera, Delphinus, and Pteropus all possess mammary glands, hair on the skin, respiration by lungs, a four-chambered heart, homoiothermy, and viviparity. They do not use gills or pneumatic bones.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
They are placed in Class Mammalia because they possess mammary glands, hair, lung respiration, and a four-chambered heart.

answer.text: Gill respiration in aquatic forms and pneumatic bones in flying forms
Mammary glands, hair on the skin, lung respiration, and a four-chambered heart

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q48 - Multi-criteria phylum identification from Table 4.2

questiontext.text: An animal specimen exhibits organ-system level of organisation, bilateral symmetry, a true coelom, absence of body segmentation, a complete digestive system, and both circulatory and respiratory systems. To which phylum could this specimen belong?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phyla can be uniquely narrowed down by combining their level of organisation, symmetry, coelom, segmentation, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory features.

Step 2: Application
1. Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata are eliminated because they exhibit segmentation.
2. Aschelminthes is eliminated because it is pseudocoelomate and lacks circulatory and respiratory systems.
3. Mollusca (as well as Hemichordata) possesses organ-system level of organisation, bilateral symmetry, true coelom, no segmentation, complete digestive system, and both circulatory and respiratory systems.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The specimen belongs to Phylum Mollusca.
